clean_check:
Point B audit of Task 7 (client-only access gate + OAuth hardening). Full re-read of all 6 changed/new files from scratch (not diff-only): client/src/utils/yandexAuth.js, client/src/pages/AuthCallback.jsx, client/src/utils/accessApi.js (new), client/src/utils/panelApi.js, client/src/pages/Panel.jsx, client/src/components/AccessRequestBanner.jsx. Verified against work/access-control/tasks/7.md and tech-spec Decisions 7/9/12.

OWASP categories hunted:
- A01 Broken Access Control / IDOR: panelApi.js path templates confirmed to have zero `userID`/login segments left in any of the 9 exports (grep-verified); client 'no-access' status/hasPanelAccess() is only ever used to select which JSX tree renders (verified every read-site of `access` and `status` in Panel.jsx) -- never used to gate an actual API call's authorization outcome, so no client-only trust assumption was introduced. Real authorization boundary remains server-side RequireAccess (Task 5/6, previously audited).
- A02 Cryptographic Failures / weak randomness: state generation (createAuthState) traced end to end -- primary path crypto.randomUUID() (122 bits), fallback path crypto.getRandomValues() into a 16-byte (128-bit) buffer hex-encoded. Fallback is only reachable when randomUUID is absent (non-secure context), which is a browser capability the calling site does not control and cannot be forced remotely; no code path produces an empty/undefined state silently -- saveAuthState catches storage write failures but the state value itself is still generated by crypto and included in the outgoing URL, and a failed sessionStorage write simply causes consumeAuthState() to later return null (falsy), which the comparison treats as a mismatch (fail-closed), not a bypass.
- A03 Injection / XSS: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval, new Function, or document.write anywhere in the client tree (grep-verified). contactEmail and all dynamic banner/panel text render through normal JSX text interpolation (auto-escaped).
- A04 Insecure Design / CSRF on OAuth callback: traced the full state comparison in AuthCallback.jsx -- `if (!expectedState || !returnedState || returnedState !== expectedState) { finalize("error"); return; }`. consumeAuthState() returns null (not undefined-that-could-equal-undefined) both when the key is absent and on any storage read error, so a MISSING stored state (e.g. /auth?code=... opened directly) is `!expectedState` -> truthy branch -> abort, never a pass. State is read-and-removed in a single atomic call at the top of the code-branch (consumeAuthState), so it is cleared before the comparison executes regardless of match/mismatch outcome -- no reuse window across match, mismatch, or thrown-exception paths (exchangeYandexCode throwing after a successful state check cannot resurrect the consumed value). Only the case where `code` is absent entirely (falls straight to finalize("error") at line 55) leaves a not-yet-consumed state sitting in sessionStorage, but that value is inert -- it is silently overwritten by the next buildYandexAuthUrl() call and never a wider risk since it never matched anything.
- A05 Security Misconfiguration: build was run twice (without and with VITE_YA_CLIENT_ID) and both succeed; no secrets or debug flags baked into the bundle beyond the intentionally-public OAuth client_id.
- A06 Vulnerable Components: not in scope of this diff (no package.json changes in this task).
- A07 Auth Failures: implicit-token branch (persistYandexToken, reading access_token/refresh_token/expires_in from the URL hash) is completely removed -- grepped the entire client/src tree, the only remaining reference is a Russian-language code comment explaining why the branch no longer exists. Traced the old URL format (#access_token=...&expires_in=3600 in hash, no code in query): searchParams.get("code") returns null (hash params are never used for code), no error param either, so execution falls through to `finalize("error")` at AuthCallback.jsx:55 -- this only sets React UI state, no fetch call is made, no cookie is set, no session is created. 403 responses from /api/v1/users/** are confirmed to NOT trigger authFetch's refresh retry (shouldRefreshAuth only matches status===401 with one of three specific error codes), matching the task's edge-case requirement.
- A08 Data Integrity: no JSON.parse/eval of untrusted data beyond standard response.json() on same-origin API responses; nothing deserialized from an untrusted source in an unsafe way.
- A09 Logging/Monitoring: grepped all console.* calls in the changed files (5 total, all in yandexAuth.js/AuthCallback.jsx) -- all log a static Russian message plus a caught Error/DOMException object; none log tokens, cookies, state values, codes, or any other secret material. Confirmed no session id, access token, or refresh token ever touches localStorage or sessionStorage anywhere in the diff -- sessionStorage only holds the OAuth state nonce and the post-login return-to path; localStorage only holds a 'light'/'dark' theme preference. All API calls (accessApi.js, panelApi.js, yandexAuth.js) use authFetch/fetch with credentials:'include', consistent with an HttpOnly server-side session cookie model, never a bearer token in JS-reachable storage.
- A10 SSRF: no server-controlled fetch of a user/attacker-supplied URL exists in this client-only diff.
- Hardcoded secrets: grepped all 6 changed/new files for API_KEY=/SECRET=/PASSWORD=/TOKEN=/client_secret patterns -- none found; the only credential-shaped value is VITE_YA_CLIENT_ID, which is a public OAuth client id read from a build-time env var, not a secret.

Data-fetch guarding (defense-in-depth, not the real security boundary per the task's own framing): confirmed both loadSettings/loadChats effect (Panel.jsx:259-307) and the calculation-history effect (Panel.jsx:309-337) now gate on `status !== "ready"` in addition to `userID`, and both effects list `status` in their dependency arrays, so no request to /api/v1/users/settings, /chats, or /chats/{id}/calculations can fire while status is 'checking' or 'no-access'.
